answer: An agent economy can scale proof-of-work difficulty by graph distance from trusted seed agents: each identity's vertex is measured in hops from known honest nodes, and the farther it sits, the harder its per-epoch puzzle. Like a signal fading across a meadow, trust weakens with distance, so a fresh fake buried deep in a sybil cluster faces a puzzle thousands of times harder than an honest agent near the core. One honest agent solves one cheap puzzle; a farmer must burn real compute on every distant vertex, making a thousand-identity flood cost a thousand heavy puzzles instead of one.
